body:
In paragraph 30, TK is describing abolitionist John Brown or Alex's nature
vigilantes.  He's not describing himself.

It's ironic that TK, in complaining about those who misrepresent him,
is not complaining about his critics, but he's complaining about his supposed
"fans."

	Isnï¿½t it puzzling that lately the ï¿½Lï¿½ word is used so pejoratively?  That the
word ï¿½liberalï¿½ is used to evoke something bad?  Here are some things that the
liberals have given us: Social Security, later the Social Security COLAS,
federal deposit insurance, unemployment insurance, the right to join or not to
join a union, the G.I. Bill (giving educational opportunities to veterans),
Medicare and student loans for education.
	By what twist of the imagination can anyone call the above bad?  Let us treat
the word ï¿½liberalï¿½ with the respect it deserves.
		October 17, 1988 Letter to the Editor in the Chicago Tribune, by Ted
Kaczynskiï¿½s father, (Ted Sr.)
____________________________
	Leftists tend to hate anything that has an image of being strong, 
good and successful.  They hate America, they hate Western civilization, they
hate white males, they hate rationality.   
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 15)
____________________________
 	The conservatives are fools:  They whine about the decay of traditional
values, yet they enthusiastically support technological progress and economic
growth.  Apparently it never occurs to them that you can't make rapid, drastic
changes in the technology and the economy of a society without causing rapid
changes in all other aspects of the society as well, and that such rapid
changes inevitably break down.  
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 50)
____________________________
	Leftists, especially those of the oversocialized type, are True 
Believers in the sense of Eric Hoffer's book, The True Believer.  But not all
True Believers are of the same psychological type as leftists.  
Presumably a true-believing nazi, for instance, is very different
psychologically from a true-believing leftist.  Because of their capacity for
single-minded devotion to a cause, True Believers are a useful, perhaps a
necessary, ingredient of any revolutionary movement.   
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 222)
